judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Dry, cynical townsfolk ('The smart people have already left... Let them take it, I say') in short flat sentences; the panic line is a touch generic but the deadpan is Nox's.

items.label: B
items.critique: 'March on, Wanderer' and 'foul Ogres' / 'garrison's spears' is heroic-fantasy register Nox's villagers rarely use; the coined form of address gives it away.

items.label: C
items.critique: The cackling digger has Nox's oddball touch, but 'friend Wanderer' and the run-on 'deep shafts then they come for the town' read as an imitation of the voice.

items.label: D
items.critique: Three curt lines, one snub ('I'm very busy.'), a plain hint about hostile forest creatures; exactly Nox's terse filler-NPC rhythm.

items.label: E
items.critique: Lava taunt and the ellipsis-broken 'My tools... taken... every last one' are written to be dramatic; the rumour line ('Odd things happening around here lately') is filler that points at a quest hook too neatly.

items.label: F
items.critique: Folksy warning about taverns, a bare 'Beware of the rising undead,' and a gameplay tip about fire-walking boots: the plain, slightly silly hint-giving of Nox's towns.

items.label: G
items.critique: The wry aside about a villainess having style, the breathless 'They're here!' and 'Only fools and warriors' carry Nox's humour and town-gossip voice.

items.label: H
items.critique: Pure signposting (mayor's house, little boat behind the inn, inn on your left, thanks for a rescue); functional but lacks any character, and 'telling everyone about it' is flat.

items.label: I
items.critique: Gossipy alarm with a comic detail (mayor deathly afraid of spiders), the double-dash and the uncorrected 'off you back' typo feel like shipped 1999 text.

items.label: J
items.critique: Leech yelp and urchin sighting are Nox-like slapstick, but 'You're thinking of my brother, sorry' is a context-less oddity and 'Ew!' sounds modern; a close call.

tells: Invented honorific forms of address ('Wanderer', 'friend Wanderer') recur in the new texts; Nox's townsfolk mostly say nothing to the player or use 'stranger'/'Adventurer'.
New texts lean on epic register ('foul', 'March on', 'spears') or on dramatic ellipses; Westwood's lines are deadpan, gossipy, and often comic or cynical.
New texts over-signpost (directions to the inn, boat, mayor's house) in tidy, complete sentences; Westwood's hints are blunter and stranger, often a single tip or warning.
Westwood lines include snubs and non-sequiturs ('I'm very busy.') and occasional typos; new texts are cleaner and more purposeful.
Modern interjections ('Ew!') and run-on clauses missing a comma signal the imitation.
